I've been working this land for 40 years. I know what it needs and what I can handle at my age. My back isn't what it was, and it's just me and my wife now, so I keep things manageable.

My 9.5 mu splits naturally: about 8 mu stays in my wheat-maize rotation — same fields, same sequence I've followed my whole life. I keep about 1.5 mu for cotton. Cotton prices have been decent and I know how to grow it, but I won't expand it because I can't manage the picking on my own anymore.

**Wheat:** I sow in mid-October after maize harvest. I'll use the Jimai improved variety the seed station sells — not the new hybrid stuff that costs more. I apply base fertilizer before sowing and topdress at jointing. Three irrigations: one before sowing to settle the soil, one before winter freeze, one at jointing. That's what I always do. Two pesticide passes — herbicide early spring and one for aphids and rust before heading. I rotary till after maize to break up the stubble.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June, I seed directly into the field — no-tillage, saves me labor and fuel. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 type, same as my neighbors. Maize gets more nitrogen than wheat. Summer rains help but I'll irrigate twice if it's dry — once at seedling stage and once at silking. Two pesticide applications for weeds and corn borer.

**Cotton:** I plough this small plot in spring. Hybrid or improved seed from the market. Cotton needs more water and more spraying — I'll irrigate four times and spray five times for bollworm, aphids, mites. It's tiring work but I know it well and the income is worth it for 1.5 mu.
